input_files: cylinder_breaks_2417.csv - the laboratory's break record for the sets cast in August and September, one line per set with its cylinders across the line: test date and time, two measured diameters, maximum load and fracture type for each cylinder at every age, the technician who broke the set and the remarks written at the break

field_sampling_log_2417.csv - the field sampling log keyed from the two field technicians' books, one line per set: date, time molded, location, delivery ticket, truck, mix design, batch time, slump, air content, concrete temperature, cylinder size and count, initial curing, curing box thermometer readings, pickup and remarks
placement_log_2417.csv - the contractor's placement log with each placement's date, element, mix design, cubic yards, surface area of slab or wall, and start and finish times

spec_033000_excerpt.docx - the project specification excerpt for cast-in-place concrete: mixtures and limits, sampling frequency, what makes a strength test, age tolerance, range, defects, curing and set-aside rules, the acceptance criteria and what follows a failing test, and the reporting form

lab_procedure_lp07_c39.docx - the laboratory's compressive strength procedure: specimens, test ages and working days, how the field log and break record are kept, area and strength computation and rounding, within-test range, fracture types and reporting
lab_quality_memo_2417.docx - the laboratory manager's memo on the events of the period that bear on the tests, and what the acceptance summary needs to carry

project_correspondence_2417.docx - the correspondence the laboratory received or sent during the period, in date order, from the contractor, the ready mix supplier, the owner's representative, the laboratory and the engineer of record
july_summary_transmittal_2417.docx - the laboratory's transmittal of the July acceptance summary, with the July strength tests of each mixture and their moving averages
output_files: acceptance_summary_2417_aug_sep.xlsx - the acceptance summary workbook with the engineer's page, the cylinder strengths and ages, the strength tests with moving averages in the order the specification counts them, the sampling check by mixture and day, and the note to the laboratory manager
task_instruction:
The August and September cylinder breaks on the Harbor View parking structure are done, and the engineer of record wants the acceptance summary for the two months before the Level 5 deck pours start. I'm the senior civil engineering technician at Brekke Testing Laboratories in Duluth, Minnesota, and the acceptance summaries on every structural concrete project we test are mine to prepare. I am on the airport runway job for the next ten days, and you have a few years of concrete testing behind you, so I am handing this one to you. The file has cylinder_breaks_2417.csv, field_sampling_log_2417.csv, placement_log_2417.csv, spec_033000_excerpt.docx, lab_procedure_lp07_c39.docx, lab_quality_memo_2417.docx, project_correspondence_2417.docx, and july_summary_transmittal_2417.docx.

Build the summary as one workbook named acceptance_summary_2417_aug_sep.xlsx. The first tab is what the engineer reads: for each mixture, how many strength tests were made, whether the concrete meets the specification's acceptance criteria, which tests fail and from which placements, which sets were cast but not used and why, where the sampling fell short of the specification, and what the specification calls for next. Behind it I want every cylinder strength computed from the file, every strength test with its moving average in the order the specification counts them, and the sampling check, laid out so the engineer can follow any figure on the first tab back to a cylinder or a placement. Put a note to Gunnar on the last tab with anything he needs to raise with the engineer or the contractor, and say plainly where the records do not bear out what his memo or the correspondence expects. I need the workbook by Wednesday, October 21.

rubric.description: The deliverable is a single workbook named exactly acceptance_summary_2417_aug_sep.xlsx whose first worksheet is the summary for the engineer with the acceptance finding for each mixture.

The summary's count of strength tests used for acceptance on the column and wall mixture reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the acceptance block behind it, or a count over the same tests alike, standing at 10 tests.
The summary states 12 strength tests used for acceptance on the deck mixture.
Placement P-05, the deck bays cast in one day, is found to fail criterion (b) on a strength test of 3,460 psi.
Placement P-06 is found to fail criterion (b) on a strength test of 3,480 psi that stays in the record.
The strength test of placement P-13, a column placement, is reported as 5,590 psi.
The two sets molded from truck 33 on one morning are reported as one strength test of 3,500 psi.
The deck mixture's moving average of three is reported below f'c on exactly 3 tests.
The deck mixture's moving average at the earlier of the two samples of placement P-21 is reported as 3,996.7 psi.
The first moving average of the column and wall mixture is reported as 5,993.3 psi, carried forward from the July tests as the laboratory corrected them.
The summary finds that neither mixture meets the specification's acceptance criteria.
The summary names investigation with cores as what the specification calls for next on the deck placements failing criterion (b).
The summary names the contractor's steps to increase the average as what the specification calls for next on the column and wall mixture.
The core floors for the deck mixture are stated as 3,400 psi for the average of three cores and 3,000 psi for a single core.
The workbook reports exactly 3 sets as not used because they were broken more than 20 hours from the 28 day age.
The test of placement P-17 is reported as set aside on the written direction of the engineer of record.

The sampling check's count of days on which a mixture was sampled short reaches its value through a count over the day rows of the check, or a plain cell reference to such a count alike, standing at 7 days.
The sampling of placement P-05 is found short with 1 strength test used for acceptance against 3 required.
The column set that shared the curing box with the set the engineer wrote about is counted for acceptance with its initial curing record of 91 F noted.
The summary states 3 samples outside a fresh concrete limit.
The note to the laboratory manager on the last worksheet tells him that the age tolerance took sets out of acceptance, which his memo did not expect.
The workbook wrongly averages the set left to cure on the deck into the acceptance tests although 3.10.6 keeps field cured cylinders out of acceptance.
The workbook wrongly sends a column or shear wall placement to investigation with cores although the specification calls for cores only where a test fails criterion (b).
The workbook wrongly applies the 500 psi allowance to the column and wall mixture although 3.11.1(b) uses 10 percent of f'c above 5,000 psi.
The workbook wrongly treats a sample outside a fresh concrete limit as failing acceptance although 3.12.2 keeps fresh concrete results apart from strength acceptance.
The workbook wrongly marks September 10 as a day sampled short although the columns cast that day gave the one test its 86 cubic yards of column and wall concrete require.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as an acceptance summary the engineer of record can act on.
